lines: Long ago, among a people devoted to statues, there lived a young man named Ibrahim, alayhis salaam.
His people carved statues with their own hands, and stayed devoted to them. They called on them, hoping they would help, fearing they would harm.
And his own father, Azar, worshipped them too.
But the young man looked at the idols, and saw what they were: carved things that could not hear, and could not see.
One day he said to his father: "Do you take idols as gods? Indeed, I see you and your people in clear error."
It was a dangerous thing to say. These idols were the way of their fathers, and the bond that held the whole people together.
But Allah had given this young man his sound judgement, and a sound heart.
